note: Synthetic memory entries and queries for M1. Expected lists the entries that should rank in the top three, best first.
entries: Invoices use the format INV-YYYY-NNNN and restart each January.
Send every invoice in US dollars, even for customers abroad.
Remind customers about unpaid invoices after 14 days, then weekly.
Reach 120k in revenue by the end of the third quarter.
Hire two engineers and one designer in Q1.
The mobile app launches in the fourth quarter, after the beta closes.
Releases are cut from main and tagged vX.Y.Z; never release from a feature branch.
Avoid releasing on Fridays: the last two Friday releases needed weekend fixes.
Every release needs notes written for customers, not a commit list.
Keep meetings to 25 minutes and send the agenda the day before.
No meetings on Wednesdays; that day is for focused work.
The daily standup moved to 9:30 from 10:00.
Annual recurring revenue: monthly recurring revenue times twelve.
Customers who cancelled during the month divided by customers at its start.
Back up the production database every night and keep 30 days of copies.
Test restoring a backup every month; a backup nobody restored is a guess.
Store passwords hashed with argon2id; never log them.
API keys live in the keychain or the secret store, never in the repository.
Keep pull requests under 400 changed lines so they can be reviewed in one sitting.
A pull request merges only when its tests pass locally.
Unit tests use vitest; end-to-end tests use playwright.
Commit messages say what changed and why, in the imperative.
A company with at least one paid seat.
Interview five customers each month about onboarding.
Most new customers stop at connecting their calendar; make that step optional.
Weekly reports lead with the three numbers that changed most, then the reasons.
The monthly finance report includes revenue, churn and cash on hand.
Flights over 600 dollars need approval before booking.
Book hotels within walking distance of the office being visited.
Mockups are made in the shared canvas, not in slides.
Every screen must work in dark mode before it ships.
Text contrast meets WCAG AA and every control has a label.
Should team plans be priced per seat or per workspace?
The individual plan costs 12 dollars a month, billed yearly.
Discount codes over 30 percent attracted customers who churned within two months.
Support answers within four business hours, Monday to Friday.
Support replies are short, name the fix first and avoid apologies longer than a line.
Refunds within 30 days need no reason; later ones go to the owner.
Send the product newsletter on the first Tuesday of each month.
Social posts show the product working; no stock photos.
Launch emails sent on Tuesday mornings got the most replies.
Customer data stays in the US region.
Logs are kept for 14 days and never contain message text.
Error messages say what happened and what to do next, without codes.
One person who can sign in to a workspace.
Bring monthly churn under 3 percent by the end of Q4.
Estimates for new features ran about twice as long as planned; add a buffer.
Plan work in two-week cycles that start on Mondays.
Shared numbers live in one spreadsheet per team, not in chat.
